items.title: Euthyna ESG platform
items.summary: AI sustainability-reporting SaaS. His work covers disclosure gap analysis, GHG calculations, climate risk and transition planning, plus GHG boundary-setting and ownership extraction.
story: Euthyna turns sustainability disclosures into structured data. On the product side, a report goes in and comes back as a gap analysis with compliance checks and recommendations; the frameworks it analyses against are listed on euthyna.ai.

The GHG side needs survey flows to collect sustainability data, organisational and operational boundary-setting in the GHG Protocol style, and ownership extraction, which maps equity and control relationships for consolidation.

Under that sit LLM-driven estimation pipelines, background processing, RBAC and transactional audit logging. The org-standard stack is React + Vite, NestJS/Express, PostgreSQL, Drizzle, Zod, CASL and React Query.

The CRM replaces the existing outreach stack through a Lemlist integration. The project-management and finance tools handle internal operations.

items.title: MotionIQ
items.summary: A human-activity-recognition data system. An Android app streams phone IMU data over Wi-Fi into RabbitMQ, a Java consumer drains the queues, and a Python pipeline cuts atomic 5-second windows.
story: The mobile app is simple on purpose: set the server address and port, pick the sensors, press start. Readings stream over Wi-Fi to a RabbitMQ broker, and a Java consumer processes the queues.

The preprocessing pipeline runs in 8 steps. It standardises subject and activity names, restructures the recordings, converts them to atomic 5-second JSON windows, exports a raw CSV dataset and segments falls from daily activities.

Around the pipeline sit fixer scripts for sync and event renaming, plots comparing users, sensors and subjects, gravity calculation from the IMUs, and verification tools such as a sensor-rate counter.

items.title: Kickstart HQ
items.summary: Field-service management: scheduling, dispatching, invoicing, technicians and payments. Response time went from 27s to 3.5s.
story: Kickstart HQ runs field-service businesses end to end, from scheduling and dispatching technicians to invoicing and payments.
The work was performance. webpack optimisation, code splitting and compression, plus lazy loading and fewer API calls, took response time from 27s to 3.5s.

items.title: Structure Fetcher
items.summary: Upload an org chart as an image or PDF and get the hierarchy back as editable JSON, extracted by Azure OpenAI or Groq vision models.
story: The Express API sends uploaded charts to Azure OpenAI or Groq, validates the hierarchy that comes back, stores it in MongoDB and keeps files on Cloudinary. Winston logs rotate daily.
The React + Vite frontend offers drag-and-drop upload, an interactive tree view and a table view, inline edit, add and delete of entities, saving to the backend, and JSON export.
